earlier_scan.note: Extinct Tupi (Arikem branch); only Rondon Commission wordlists (Rondon & Faria 1948 glossario); no grammar or phonology found.

sources.citation: Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú, language page 'Arikém' (etnolinguistica.org/lingua:arikem), listing Badet 1951, Rondon 1916, Rondon & Faria 1948, Nimuendajú 1932.
sources.note: Bibliographic listing only; confirms the documentary record for Arikém proper is wordlists/ethnographic notes.

sources.citation: Rondon, Cândido M. S. & João Barbosa de Faria. 1948. Glossário geral das tribos silvícolas de Mato-Grosso e outras da Amazônia e do Norte do Brasil, Tomo I. Rio de Janeiro: CNPI. ('Vocabulário da língua Ariquême (úitá)', p.193ff, collected by J. Barbosa de Faria, rio Jamari, 24 Jan 1927).
sources.note: No rule stated. Front-matter item IV (p.12): 'A acentuação que aparece, aplicada a vogais, em alguns vocabulários... corresponde aos sons fortes e longos de sílabas tônicas.' The Ariquême vocabulary marks an accented vowel on most items (e.g. Corombó 'boca', Opixáua 'cabelo', Pioçó 'calcanhar') but gives no statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon D. 1999. Tupí. In Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages, 107-124. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Nothing on Arikém proper; for the branch only the Karitiana remark (§2.3): 'In Karitiana and in languages of the Tupari branch there is salient pitch accent, but it is predictable from stress which is itself predictable from other phonological and morphological factors.' Arikém-branch discussion is limited to the vowel shift and vowel length.

sources.citation: Storto, Luciana R. 1999. Aspects of a Karitiana grammar. PhD dissertation, MIT.
sources.note: Describes Karitiana (sister language) stress/pitch accent only; mentions Arikém only as the family name and cites Storto & Baldi 1994 'The Proto-Arikem Vowel Shift' (LSA paper, ms.). No statement about Arikém-language stress.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1932. Wortlisten aus Amazonien. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 24(1): 93-119 (III. Arikém, pp. 109-116; consultant Pará from Rio Candeias, recorded Manaus 1926).
sources.note: No rule stated. Transcription key (p.93 'Diakritische Zeichen') marks the stressed vowel per item: acute = 'tontragender Vokal'; the Arikém list (pp.109-116) carries these per-word stress marks but no prose on accent placement.
